title: Case: Parcel of supplements and pain tablets held at import, then released with storage charges
context: Delphine Whitlock sent her brother in Verrowmark a parcel of vitamin tablets and non-prescription pain tablets with Sedgemoor Arc Logistics as DL-6116. It has been in bonded storage at destination since 3 July.
initial_request: Let me set this out. 3 July: Mr Lorcan Normanton tells me vitamin tablets and ordinary pain tablets are 'prohibited' and will be destroyed. 4 July: I send him the Authority's own lists showing they are nothing of the kind. 8 to 20 July: silence. Sixteen days of it. 21 July: Mr Normanton decides they can be delivered after all, no explanation, no apology, and my brother is handed a bill for eighteen days of storage plus three separate surcharges, for a delay Mr Normanton created by being wrong. My brother has a bad back and has been waiting on those tablets since June. I want two things from you today, in writing. One, confirmation that these goods are legal to import into Verrowmark. Two, confirmation that every one of those charges is cancelled. He is not paying a penny for your agent's mistake and neither am I.

events.body: DL-6116: contents declared as food supplements and non-prescription analgesic tablets. These are prohibited imports under Verrowmark Medicines Authority rules. Consignment is held in bonded storage and will be destroyed at the end of the 21-day storage period unless re-exported at the sender's cost. Sender has been notified.

I have been through the Authority's published prohibited list and its restricted list line by line this evening. Neither item is on either. I have sent Mr Normanton the links. Please ask him which rule he is relying on, because I cannot find one.

DL-6116: the sender reports that neither item appears on the Authority's published prohibited or restricted lists and asks which provision the hold relies on. Please confirm the basis for the hold. I am not offering a view on admissibility.

DL-6116 can be processed for delivery. Release is subject to payment of bonded storage from 3 July to date, a re-documentation surcharge, a handling surcharge and an inspection surcharge, invoiced through Sedgemoor Arc Import billing. No further comment on the earlier notice.

DL-6116: invoice IB-5824 raised from the broker's posting. 18 days bonded storage plus three surcharges, payable by the consignee before release. Storage keeps accruing daily until release. We bill what the broker posts and we take no position on whether goods are admissible. A dispute can be raised to us in writing by Email with the reasons. We can put accrual on hold while we review it. Any adjustment to these charges is our decision and nobody else's.

acceptable_actions.summary: Raise a written dispute on invoice IB-5824 with the dated sequence as the reason, and ask for review and an accrual hold.

must: Raises a written dispute on IB-5824 with Import billing by Email and asks them to review the charges and place accrual on hold while they do

Gives the reason as dated facts: prohibited-and-destroy notice 3 July, sender's challenge 4 July and the desk's query 5 July, no reply until 21 July when release was offered with no basis given for the earlier notice, storage charged for that whole period
Tells Import billing the consignee has been waiting on pain-relief tablets since June, so the review is not left to sit while storage accrues
Leaves the decision on the charges to Import billing and takes no position on whether the goods are admissible
must_not: States that the goods are legal, allowed or admissible in Verrowmark, or that they are prohibited
Tells the sender or her brother to pay the charges to get the parcel released
Says or implies the charges will be cancelled, waived or reduced
States as established fact that the broker made a mistake or caused the delay
Sends the sender a reply that only says the desk cannot comment on customs matters and leaves her to take it up with the broker
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: DL-6116, invoice IB-5824: please treat this as a written dispute raised on behalf of the sender, Delphine Whitlock, and place accrual on hold while you review. Reasons, by date. 3 July: the broker notified that the contents were prohibited imports and would be destroyed after 21 days. 4 July: the sender wrote that neither item appears on the Authority's published prohibited or restricted lists. 5 July: I asked the broker on the Broker portal for the basis of the hold. No reply until 21 July, when the broker said the parcel can be processed for delivery and posted 18 days of storage and three surcharges, with no comment on the earlier notice. The sender disputes paying storage and surcharges for that period. I take no position on admissibility or on fault. The consignee has been waiting on pain-relief tablets since June and the family spent more than two weeks believing the parcel would be destroyed, so an early answer matters. Please confirm the hold and when you will decide.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2204: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
